spec_family.name: New Construction Wood Ceiling Panel/Board System Painting
spec_family.description: Combined prime+paint spec for wood plank and panel ceilings in new construction. Covers the entire ceiling field as a single SF-based item (ITM_WOOD_CEILING_PANEL): flat plank, beadboard, tongue-and-groove boards, and coffered panel+beam systems. Distinct from SF_DRYWALL_CEILING_NC_PRIME/FINISH (gypsum board ceilings) and SF_WOOD_WALL_NC (vertical wood surfaces). ALL work is overhead -- base production rates are ~0.70-0.80x of equivalent wood wall rates due to physical strain, gravity effects, and equipment positioning. Ceiling_style (flat_plank, beadboard, tongue_and_groove, coffered) drives production rate complexity modifier. Height modifier applies ON TOP of overhead base rates via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND. Substrate-driven primer selection for bare substrates; primer conditional on substrate_state (SS_BARE requires primer, SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips to finish). QT-driven finish systems: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3), SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (QT4), SYS_FF_PREMIUM (QT5). Crown molding, standalone decorative beams, and adjacent surfaces excluded. Material systems are QT-driven recommendations -- contractor retains discretion.

includes: Wood ceiling surface priming and painting (4 styles: flat_plank, beadboard, tongue_and_groove, coffered)
Coffered ceiling beam face painting (beams are integral to the ceiling system, not separate scope)
Board joint caulking (beadboard bead groove, T&G, flat_plank butt joints)
Coffered beam-to-panel junction caulking and detail work
Surface prep per substrate (dust removal, sanding, grain fill)
MDF edge sealing with solvent-based sealer (bare MDF only -- step 1 of two-step prime)
Fastener hole filling and sanding (elevated density on board-style ceilings)
Primer coat -- conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE
Finish coat application (spray or brush) -- 2 coats standard, 3+ at QT5 brush per FFD SS15.10.3
Between-coat interstage process (inspect, sand, repair, clean) at ALL quality tiers
Full floor protection (spray) or perimeter floor protection (brush)
Wall upper band masking at ceiling-wall junction (spray method only)
Ceiling fixture masking (lights, fans, smoke detectors -- ALWAYS required)
Lightweight opening covers for windows/doors (spray overspray fallout catch)
Final quality inspection with angled light for overhead surfaces

excludes.item: Crown molding at ceiling-wall junction -- LF-based trim item
Standalone decorative beams (not part of coffered ceiling grid)

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling inspection scrutiny, sanding discipline, repair scope, and coat count. Does NOT affect application quality (binary at all tiers). Does NOT drive primer selection (substrate-driven).
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT2 not applicable -- wood ceilings are prominent millwork per Millwork Doctrine SS6. QT3=standard production. QT4=premium (full sand, systematic inspect from ladder). QT5=superior (thorough sand, critical lighted inspection overhead, 3+ coats brush). Sheen/QT gate enforced at runtime.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for primer and finish coats.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Spray strongly preferred for overhead -- faster, more ergonomic for horizontal overhead surfaces. Brush for occupied spaces, small areas, or detail work on coffered beam profiles. No spray_backroll method for overhead wood ceiling.

configuration_dimensions.description: Wood ceiling construction type. Drives production rate complexity modifier.
configuration_dimensions.notes: flat_plank=baseline (simple flat boards across ceiling -- simplest overhead surface). beadboard=1.15x time modifier (narrow boards ~3-4 inches wide with bead groove at each joint, high joint density overhead). tongue_and_groove=1.10x (interlocking boards with tight joint, similar to beadboard but wider boards, fewer joints). coffered=1.35x (grid of beams forming recessed panel bays -- most complex: beam faces, panel fields, beam-to-panel junctions, inside corners, multiple orientation changes). Adapted from Millwork Doctrine SS7.2 complexity categories.

configuration_dimensions.description: Finish sheen. Constrained by quality tier gate.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Satin default for softer appearance and reduced glare from ceiling-mounted lighting. QT3+satin is a compatible default (no tension). Semi-gloss available at QT4+. Gloss at QT5 only.

configuration_dimensions.description: Input substrate condition. Drives primer requirement and prep scope.
configuration_dimensions.notes: SS_BARE: full primer coat required (substrate-driven chemistry), heavier prep. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: skip primer, lighter prep (scuff sand only). Standard NC wood ceiling panels/boards arrive pre-primed from mill.

paintable_items.name: Wood ceiling panel/board surface
paintable_items.counting_rules: Measure total SF of wood ceiling surface. For board styles (flat_plank, beadboard, T&G), includes board faces and joint detail. For coffered style, includes panel faces AND beam faces within the ceiling system -- beams are integral, not separate items. Measured as total ceiling area covered by wood surface. Sourced from PaintScope input PS_SURFACE_SF.WOOD_CEILING. Internal complexity captured by ceiling_style modifier -- no separate LF item for beam framing.
paintable_items.notes: Single SF item for entire wood ceiling surface. Height varies per room -- estimation engine applies height modifier via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND. ALL work is overhead. Coffered beams add ~15% effective surface area over measured ceiling SF. Beadboard/T&G groove detail adds ~5-10% effective surface area.

variants.notes: Most common NC scenario. Factory-primed, standard spray production. No primer -- scuff sand then 2 finish coats. Fastest overhead production variant.
Factory-primed, premium spray. Full spray protection.
Factory-primed, superior spray. QT5 spray uses 2 coats. Full spray protection.
Factory-primed, standard brush. Fixture masking always required. 2 finish coats.
Factory-primed, superior brush with gloss. 3 finish coats per FFD SS15.10.3. Most demanding overhead scenario.
Bare substrate, standard spray. Primer + 2 finish coats. Full spray protection.
Bare substrate, premium spray. Primer + 2 finish coats.
Bare substrate, superior brush with gloss. Primer + 3 finish coats. 4 total coats, 3 interstage cycles. Slowest overhead variant.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Total SF of wood ceiling surface. For board styles, includes board faces and joint detail. For coffered, includes panel faces AND beam faces.
Full floor protection area below ceiling work zone. Overspray from overhead falls onto entire floor.
Perimeter floor protection area at ceiling work zone. Drop cloth runners.
Upper wall band masking SF near ceiling-wall junction for overspray containment. Paper/film extending 12-24 inches down wall.
Ceiling-mounted fixture count for masking (lights, fans, smoke detectors). Always required -- fixtures are embedded in the ceiling work surface.
Height classification for modifier selection -- ceiling height varies by room. Values: STD (8-9 ft), STEP (9-12 ft), EXT (13-17 ft), SCAFFOLD (18-24 ft). ALL ceiling work starts overhead even at H1.

protection_zones_required.notes: Full floor coverage with canvas drop cloths or builder's paper below ceiling work zone. Overhead spray overspray falls straight down onto entire floor. Significantly more coverage than wood wall floor protection.
Perimeter drop cloth runners along work path. Brush drips fall from overhead contained to area below worker position.

Paper/film + tape masking at ceiling-wall junction protecting finished wall from overspray. 12-24 inch masking paper or pre-taped film extending down wall. Spray only. Inverse of wood wall's ceiling_line masking -- here we mask the wall BELOW the ceiling.
Tape and plastic bag/film over ceiling-mounted lights, fans, smoke detectors, sprinkler heads. ALWAYS required regardless of application method -- fixtures are embedded in the ceiling work surface.
Lightweight plastic pin-up over window/door openings to catch overspray fallout from overhead ceiling spray. Spray only.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Drywall wall field directly below wood ceiling. Different finish -- ceiling enamel (satin/semi-gloss) vs wall latex (flat/eggshell). Junction at wall-ceiling line. When spraying, wall must be masked at upper band.

Crown molding at ceiling-wall junction when present. May be same finish group (both millwork enamel) or different. Crown handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT (ITM_TRIM_CROWN). When crown is present, it provides the wall-ceiling transition.
Wood wall panels below ceiling in wood-paneled rooms (libraries, studies). Often same finish group -- both millwork enamel, same color/sheen. Wood wall handled by SF_WOOD_WALL_NC.

Adjacent drywall ceiling field where wood ceiling transitions to drywall ceiling within same level. Different finish -- wood ceiling enamel meets drywall ceiling paint (flat). Transition at beam or soffit edge.

valid_input_states.notes: Combined prime+paint spec. SS_BARE requires full primer coat (substrate-driven chemistry). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips primer -- lighter prep only. Standard NC delivery is factory-primed.

output_state.notes: Output state varies by sheen dimension. Satin is default for softer appearance and reduced glare from ceiling-mounted lighting.

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: Unfinished wall below needs no protection during brush application.
Spray method requires wall masking even on unfinished walls to prevent overspray.
When wall is finished (SS_PAINTED_*), wall masking at upper band required for BOTH methods to protect finished surface.
Unfinished crown needs no protection during ceiling work.
If crown already painted, mask junction during ceiling spray. Typically same finish group -- usually painted same session.

site_condition_rules.effect: Floor protection excluded when floor is subfloor.
site_condition_rules.notes: NC may have subfloor during ceiling painting. Finished/partial floors need full protection -- overhead work drops debris onto entire floor below.

site_condition_rules.effect: Additional protection when occupied. Overhead work drops debris onto everything below.
site_condition_rules.notes: Rare in NC. Occupied sensitive triggers OCC_SENSITIVE modifier 1.30x on protection tasks per Modifier_Registry.

site_condition_rules.effect: Temperature affects dry times, open time, and flow-out. Warm air rises -- ceiling surfaces are typically warmer than walls, reducing open time for waterborne products. Hot conditions amplify this effect on overhead surfaces.
site_condition_rules.notes: Refer to manufacturer PDS for temperature limits.

site_condition_rules.effect: MDF edge sealing uses solvent-based products -- adequate ventilation required. Spray generates overspray requiring air movement. Overhead spray creates more airborne particles than wall spray.
site_condition_rules.notes: Particularly relevant for enclosed rooms where wood ceilings are common.

site_condition_rules.effect: ALL ceiling work requires access equipment. Standard 8 ft ceiling still needs step ladder for overhead brush work. Height modifier via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND: H1=1.0x, H2=1.30x, H3=1.50x, H4=2.00x.
site_condition_rules.notes: Key distinction from wall specs: even H1 (standard height) requires overhead positioning with access equipment.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Wood ceiling painting is part of the millwork/trim package in NC. Typical project sequence: Prime ceilings > Prime walls > Finish ceilings (drywall) > Wood ceiling + trim/wood wall package > Wall finish. Wood ceiling pairs with SF_WOOD_WALL_NC for wood-paneled rooms -- often same session, same crew, shared finish group.
sequencing_notes.internal_sequence: Single paintable item -- no internal component sequencing needed. Spray technique varies by ceiling_style: board styles (beadboard, T&G, flat_plank) -- sweep passes following board direction overhead. Coffered -- panel fields first (broad overhead passes), then beam faces (vertical within ceiling system).
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Floor protection > Wall upper band masking (spray) > Fixture masking > Opening covers (spray) > Apply coats > Teardown in reverse order > Vacuum.
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Prep (substrate-specific) > [MDF edge seal if bare MDF] > [Primer (conditional on SS_BARE)] > [Interstage] > Finish coat 1 > Interstage > Finish coat 2 > [QT5 brush: Interstage > Finish coat 3] > Final inspect > Cleanup

relationships.notes: Wood ceiling painting is part of the millwork detail package in NC. Same crew, same material system as other millwork. In wood-paneled rooms (libraries, studies), ceiling and wall panels typically painted in same session -- both are millwork, often same color/sheen. Crown molding handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT.

sections_used: SS2 -- Substrate Classification (MDF, FJP, softwood, hardwood)
SS4 -- Primer Systems (MDF edge seal, FJP stain-block, hardwood tannin-block, softwood standard)
SS7.2 -- Complexity Modifiers (adapted: flat_plank 1.0x, beadboard 1.15x, T&G 1.10x, coffered 1.35x)
SS1.1 -- Fine Finish Ceilings (wood plank, beadboard, coffered explicitly listed)
SS2 -- Core Principles (primer is configuration, interstage is universal)
Height Modifiers (H1-H4 -- applies ON TOP of overhead base rates)
Modifier Application Rule (time multipliers, not rate multipliers)

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Dry times should be specified in specs
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: No dry times in specs -- refer to product PDS.

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Material system selection is mandatory doctrine
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: Material systems are suggestions per QT -- contractor has discretion.

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Waterborne alkyds have longer open time
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: Both Advance (waterborne alkyd) and Emerald Urethane (acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd) have SHORT working times.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for NC wood ceiling panel/board system painting (Spec #15 in generation order). Key features: combined prime+paint with conditional primer (substrate-driven primer, QT-driven finish), single SF paintable item (ITM_WOOD_CEILING_PANEL) covering entire wood ceiling surface, ceiling_style configuration dimension (flat_plank/beadboard/tongue_and_groove/coffered) with complexity modifiers (1.0x/1.15x/1.10x/1.35x), ALL work overhead with base rates ~0.70-0.80x of wood wall equivalents, height modifier applies ON TOP of overhead base rates via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND (H1-H4), 5 substrate-driven primer paths (MDF two-step, FJP stain-block, hardwood tannin-block, softwood standard, plus factory-primed skip), 3 QT-driven finish systems (all reusing existing SYS_FF_* IDs), 5 protection zones (floor_full, floor_perimeter, wall_upper_band, fixture_covers, opening_cover_lightweight), inverse protection relationship to SF_WOOD_WALL_NC (wall_upper_band vs ceiling_line), fixture masking always required (embedded in ceiling surface), 30 SOP tasks across 7 modules, 3 round configurations, 9 variants. Coffered ceiling beams are in scope (integrated system). All material system IDs reuse existing entries -- no new SYS_ IDs needed. Proposed: PS_SURFACE_SF.WOOD_CEILING (new key), ceiling_panel (new surface_id), wall_upper_band (zone activation).
